title: Thalamocortical Coupling Mediates White Matter Integrity and Thalamic Morphology via DMN Connectivity in Insomnia
summary: This hypothesis proposes that thalamocortical coupling, as measured by thalamus_DMN_FC, modulates white matter integrity (FA) and thalamic morphology (thalamus_volume) in insomnia through interactions with the default mode network (DMN).
content: Thalamocortical coupling, as indexed by thalamus_DMN_FC, mediates the relationship between white matter integrity (FA) and thalamic morphology (thalamus_volume) in insomnia, with the DMN acting as a key intermediary network.
rationale: Evidence from E1-E3 shows thalamocortical coupling is linked to thalamus_DMN_FC in insomnia. E10-E12 and E4-E5 link FA (white matter integrity) and thalamus_volume (thalamic morphology) to insomnia. The DMN, as a hub for thalamocortical connectivity, may serve as a mediator between thalamocortical coupling and structural brain changes. This pathway integrates multimodal findings from EEG-fMRI, MRI, and DTI.
experimental_plan: Use regression models in insomnia patients to test the pathway: thalamus_DMN_FC (from EEG-fMRI) → FA (from DTI) → thalamus_volume (from MRI). Validate mediation using bootstrapping and compare groups with varying insomnia severity (PSQI).
novelty_assessment: Novel integration of DMN connectivity as a mediator between thalamocortical coupling and structural brain changes (FA and thalamus_volume), avoiding prior pathways that focused on direct thalamocortical effects.
key_assumptions: FA (white matter integrity) influences thalamus_volume (thalamic morphology).

metadata.directional_prediction: Higher thalamus_DMN_FC correlates with lower FA and higher thalamus_volume in insomnia.
metadata.falsification_criteria: Failure to observe mediation of FA between thalamus_DMN_FC and thalamus_volume, or no correlation between thalamus_DMN_FC and FA.

title: Thalamocortical Coupling Mediates Thalamic Morphology and Beta Power via Structural Connectivity and DMN in Insomnia
summary: This hypothesis integrates thalamocortical coupling's effects on thalamic morphology and beta power through structural connectivity and DMN interactions in insomnia, combining mechanisms from multiple top hypotheses.
content: Thalamocortical coupling modulates thalamic morphology and beta power in insomnia through structural connectivity and interactions with the default mode network (DMN). This pathway integrates structural (MRI, FA) and electrophysiological (beta power) features, linking thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC) to thalamic volume (thalamus_volume) and beta power, mediated by white matter integrity (FA) and DMN connectivity.
rationale: The evolution combines P1's DMN mediation and P3's beta power-thalamic morphology link, using P2's structural connectivity. This strengthens coherence by integrating multiple pathways and improves grounding with measurable variables (FA, thalamus_volume, beta power).
experimental_plan: Use regression models in insomnia patients to test the pathway: thalamus_DMN_FC (EEG-fMRI) → FA (DTI) → thalamus_volume (MRI) and thalamus_DMN_FC → beta_power (EEG). Validate mediation using bootstrapping and compare groups with varying insomnia severity (PSQI).
novelty_assessment: Novel integration of DMN, structural connectivity, and beta power pathways from parent hypotheses.
key_assumptions: Thalamocortical coupling affects FA and thalamus_volume through DMN interactions
FA mediates the effect of thalamocortical coupling on beta power

title: Thalamocortical Coupling Modulates Thalamic Morphology via Structural Connectivity in Insomnia
summary: This hypothesis proposes that thalamocortical coupling influences thalamic morphology through structural connectivity in insomnia, linking multimodal neuroimaging features.
content: Thalamocortical coupling modulates thalamic morphology via structural connectivity in insomnia, thereby affecting sleep quality and neuroimaging markers such as thalamus_DMN_FC and MRI structural features.
rationale: The evidence shows that thalamocortical coupling is associated with thalamus_DMN_FC in insomnia, and structural morphology is linked to MRI features. The integration of these findings suggests a pathway where thalamocortical coupling affects thalamic structure, which is supported by the existing knowledge graph connections.
experimental_plan: Use multimodal neuroimaging (EEG-fMRI and MRI) to assess thalamocortical coupling and thalamic morphology in insomnia patients. Compare thalamus_DMN_FC and MRI structural features between insomnia and control groups.
novelty_assessment: This hypothesis introduces a new pathway linking thalamocortical coupling with thalamic morphology through structural connectivity, which has not been previously highlighted in the existing hypotheses.

metadata.directional_prediction: Increased thalamocortical coupling in insomnia is associated with altered thalamic morphology as measured by MRI.
metadata.falsification_criteria: No significant correlation between thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC) and thalamic morphology (MRI) in insomnia patients.

title: Thalamic Morphology Modulates Beta Power via Structural Connectivity in Insomnia
summary: This hypothesis proposes that thalamic morphology influences beta power through structural connectivity in insomnia, linking structural and electrophysiological features.
content: Thalamic morphology modulates beta power via structural connectivity in insomnia, linking structural and electrophysiological features through thalamocortical pathways.
rationale: Evidence shows thalamic morphology is related to thalamus_volume and structural morphology, while beta power is linked to hyperarousal. Structural connectivity between thalamus and cortex may mediate this relationship, as supported by thalamocortical coupling and white matter integrity findings.
experimental_plan: Use DTI and EEG to measure structural connectivity (FA) and beta power in insomnia patients, comparing thalamus_volume and thalamocortical coupling (thalamus_DMN_FC) between groups.
novelty_assessment: Novel integration of thalamic morphology, structural connectivity, and beta power in insomnia, extending prior hypotheses that focused on thalamocortical coupling and white matter integrity.
key_assumptions: Structural connectivity mediates beta power modulation

metadata.directional_prediction: Increased thalamus_volume correlates with higher beta_power in insomnia patients with disrupted white matter integrity.
metadata.falsification_criteria: No correlation between thalamus_volume and beta_power in insomnia patients with intact white matter integrity.

title: Thalamic Morphology Modulates Slow-Wave Generation via Structural Connectivity in Insomnia
summary: This hypothesis proposes that thalamic morphology influences slow-wave generation through structural connectivity in insomnia, linking structural and electrophysiological features.
content: Thalamic morphology modulates slow-wave generation via structural connectivity in insomnia, linking structural and electrophysiological features through multimodal neuroimaging.
rationale: Evidence from the knowledge graph shows that thalamic morphology is associated with thalamus_volume and structural morphology, while slow-wave generation is linked to slow_wave_density. The integration of these features through structural connectivity provides a pathway for modulation in insomnia.
experimental_plan: Use MRI to measure thalamic morphology and EEG to measure slow-wave density. Analyze structural connectivity between thalamus and cortical regions using DTI and correlate with slow-wave density.
novelty_assessment: This hypothesis introduces a new pathway linking thalamic morphology and slow-wave generation through structural connectivity, not previously explored in existing hypotheses.
key_assumptions: Thalamic morphology is structurally connected to cortical regions involved in slow-wave generation.
Structural connectivity modulates slow-wave density in insomnia.

metadata.directional_prediction: Increased thalamic volume correlates with higher slow-wave density in insomnia patients.
metadata.falsification_criteria: No correlation between thalamus_volume and slow_wave_density in insomnia patients.
